claims.evidence: NHS: risk of neonatal herpes is higher if first caught in the last 6 weeks of pregnancy and much lower if previously had it or caught early; recurrent outbreak risk is low even with lesions at delivery. 'Outbreak at birth' framed as the risk was misleading.
claims.sentence: The risk applies if there is an outbreak at birth or the first infection happens during pregnancy.
claims.newSentence: The risk ... is higher if genital herpes is caught for the first time in the last 6 weeks of pregnancy, and is much lower for people who have had genital herpes before

claims.newSentence: The test cannot be done if there are no visible blisters or sores. (kept as NHS-sourced statement; screening/partner claims removed)

notes: 12 of 14 searches used. Author-flagged items: 'open sores' reworded (sources: painful red sores); 'repeat outbreaks milder' supported by sexual health leaflets; 'testing is free' only supported by NHS inform (Scotland), reattributed; pregnancy antiviral timing corrected to NHS ~32 weeks (BASHH leaflet 32 weeks for late first episode; trusts vary); CDC points kept, labelled US, ratio numbers omitted; NHS 111/same-day GP mapping removed. Weak points for human review: 2-12 days source is a hospital-trust page, 'two to four weeks' first-episode duration and 'recurrences milder' come from unnamed NHS sexual health leaflets; the NHS ~32 weeks statement came via a search summary and is not verified word for word; 'dry sore' sentence is from an unnamed sexual health service; screening/partner-testing claims could not be confirmed and were removed. Search summaries blend pages so attribution to nhs.uk is approximate. Sentences 3, 48, 96 and similar are counted individually.
